evidence: 200 cm chain, enters through the top 12.9 cm below y=606 at (23.8,593,270) and ends at (51.2,408,303): d_face 159.4 cm (nearest is z), 51.0 cm from the cathode, 300.9 cm from the anode face, 71.9 cm from the z=231 seam, so the end is deep in APA3 (x>0, z>232) with no exit route on the table. dy = -185 cm on a 190 cm chord, so the fit end is the lower end and rule 7 does not apply. Attached at that peak vertex is segment 142002, 10.2 cm of 18 points at 5.8e4 e/cm, i.e. back at the plateau, leaving at cos_fwd 0.84 (about 33 deg) with a kink plainly visible in two of the three stop azimuths (edge-on in the third). A muon sitting at its own Bragg peak cannot go on for another 10 cm at MIP, so 142002 is a second particle and 10 cm is the right range for a ~20 MeV Michel, whatever the chain types it. S348001 is a 2-point 0.2 cm speck at 8.0e4, 11.8 cm from the stop at cos_fwd 0.71, about 3.6 cm past the far end of the Michel arm and on the electron side: beyond the ~10 cm michel radius and detached, so gamma. notes: 348001 at 11.8 cm is the one borderline tag: it sits ~3.6 cm past the end of the Michel arm, so michel (kind attached) is a defensible alternative to gamma (kind both). Profile drops from 1.05e5 to ~5.8e4 over the last ~1 cm, which is within ordinary end scatter and much less than the several-cm sustained collapse the overshoot rule asks for, so the pin is left at the fit end.

evidence: Short 66 cm track (chain KE 179 MeV), enters the back z face at (10.4, 592.2, 460.6), 1.7 cm from z = 462 and 13.8 cm below the top, and runs down to a fit end at (24.4, 542.0, 429.6) in APA3 (x>0, z>232). dy = -50.2 over a 60.6 cm chord, a steep downward cosmic ending at its LOWER end, so rule 7 is satisfied. The end is 32.7 cm from the nearest face (z), 64 cm from the top, 24.2 cm from the cathode and 327.7 cm from the anode, and seam_z is 198.6 cm, so no face, cathode or seam is in play. The profile is the story: a 5.5-7e4 plateau from s = 45 in to s = 20, then a gradual ten-centimetre climb - 6.9e4 at s = 18, 9.3-9.8e4 at s = 16-17, 1.05e5 at s = 10.5 - to a peak of 1.29-1.33e5 at s = 9.5, i.e. twice its own plateau and following the muon reference curve. Past that peak the charge falls off a cliff: 7.2-7.5e4 at s = 7.5, 6.2e4 at s = 6, then 2.3e4, 1.6e4, 1.5e4 at s = 4.8-5.2, and it recovers only to 4.3-6.0e4 over the last 4 cm, which is at or below the plateau exactly where a stopping muon should be two to three times above it. That is the overshoot signature, so I put the pin at s = 8.5 where the muon charge leaves its peak; the collapse is narrow (about 2 cm of near-empty bridge) rather than the several cm the rule describes, which is what makes the pin the soft part of this call. Past the fit end the display shows a thin low-charge trail: 122006, 4 points over 1.9 cm sitting on the stop vertex at cos_fwd 0.51, i.e. an arm at about 60 deg, at 52284 e/cm; then 122008, 20 points running 7.65 cm straight on at 15899 e/cm, barely a quarter of the muon plateau; then 122009 at 7.7-9.3 cm at 17937. A muon cannot continue at 0.28 of MIP, so these are a second, much lighter particle - a Michel electron - and the fact that they run straight on (cos_fwd 0.91-0.96) is the weak-stub geometry but is overruled by the charge. Checked the undershoot case explicitly and it does not fit: the only hot forward piece, 339007, is 2 points at 87883 e/cm, and it sits 14.6 cm out with 9 cm of low-charge electron between it and the stop, not 1-3 cm past the end, and 1.35x plateau is not several times it. 339007 is compact, detached by a 5-6 cm charge-free gap visible in the e azimuth, and lies on the Michel side, so gamma under the beyond-10-cm rule; kind both. In f_meas the track own cells end at the fit end in all three planes; a long grey diagonal crosses the W frame right at the stop channel but sits at V 6060-6180 against the track V 6010-6050, so it is a different object passing at a different height, not a continuation and not busy enough to make this MESSY.
notes: OVERSHOOT: Bragg peak at s = 9.5 cm, charge collapses to 1.5-2.3e4 at s = 5 and never recovers above plateau, so the fit last 8.5 cm bridge the true stop to the electron; the pin move is the less certain part of this record - a competing reading makes the hot s = 8-11 stretch a delta blob and leaves the pin at the fit end, but the verdict is STM_MICHEL either way

evidence: A 765 cm straight cosmic, the longest in my set. Enters through the top at (181.2, 601.5, 30.9), 4.5 cm from y = 606, and runs down across the cathode to a fit end at (-239.8, 115.2, 355.6) in APA2 (x<0, z>232) at y = 115, above the y < 60 bottom-corner region where APA2 coverage holes bite worst. dy = -486.3 over a 720.5 cm chord (0.675), a steep downward cosmic ending at its LOWER end, so rule 7 is satisfied. The stop is contained on every axis: 106.7 cm from the nearest face (z), 107.6 cm above the floor, 112.3 cm from the anode, 239.6 cm from the cathode and 124.6 cm from the APA seam. The profile is a textbook Bragg curve and settles the item under rule 2: the plateau sits at 5.0-5.5e4 for the whole 160 cm shown, then over the last 15 cm it climbs 6.5-7.0e4 at s = 10-15, 8.0-8.7e4 at s = 5-8, 9.5-9.7e4 at s = 3-4, 1.04-1.15e5 at s = 1.5-2.5 and 1.35-1.43e5 at the last two points, i.e. 2.6 times its own plateau, tracking the muon reference curve point for point, and the 3-D colouring shows the same orange-to-red run into the star. There is no peak-then-collapse, so no overshoot and the pin stays at the fit end. Nothing at all sits past the stop: the three azimuths show a clean pencil ending at the star with only a couple of thinned context specks, and the nearest object in the table is 181 cm away - every other row (the six further chain segments, the delta 125007 and the three pdg 11 shower pieces) sits 181-720 cm back up the track near the entry, so they are all delta / other or muon and none of them is decay activity. That makes it STM_ONLY with kind none rather than STM_MICHEL. One caveat I could not resolve and have flagged: f_meas is only half usable here. The V and W panels are empty - their axes auto-ranged over 1350 and 1800 channels with no cells - so this cluster has no V or W cells in the frame, and in U the own coloured band ends at channel 2035 right where a dead-channel band runs at 2030-2040. I did not let that change the call, because a dead band cannot manufacture a smooth fifteen-centimetre climb that matches the reference curve, and a through-going muon cannot produce one either; but an auditor should know the end is at a dead band in the one plane that was drawn.
notes: DEAD: flagged for the auditor, not used as the reason - in f_meas the U fit end sits on a dead-channel band at U 2030-2040 and the V and W panels contain no cells at all for this cluster, so f_meas could only be read in one plane; the Bragg rise decides the item on its own

evidence: 334 cm chain in five segments, entering through the top at (274,605,385) just 1.3 cm below y = 606 and ending at (106.8,400.1,411.1), deep inside: d_face 51.2 cm to the z = 462 wall, 106.6 cm from the cathode, 245.3 cm from the anode and 180 cm from the z = 231 seam, in APA3 (x>0, z>232), so no exit route is on the table and neither of the two named charge deficits applies. dy = -205 cm on a 266 cm chord, so the fit end is the lower end and rule 7 does not bite. The profile, though, cannot be read: over the frame the points lie on a smooth periodic wave, zero from s = 2 to 10 cm, up to 5e4 at s = 17-19, back to zero at s = 33-36, up again to 1.7e4 near s = 40, with the markers sitting on a clean arc rather than scattering. That is the patchy-collection signature the rubric names, not a physical dQ/dx, and the giveaway that it is an artifact rather than an overshoot collapse is that the zero recurs twice inside 45 cm. The 3-D azimuths agree: the last 30-40 cm is a sparse dotted trail with only one small cloud clump at about 17 cm back, hanging off a wiggly low-charge 60 cm section (S98007 at 2.7e4, half the 6e4 plateau of the long S98010 body), and the segment means fall monotonically towards the end (6.0e4, 5.2e4, 2.7e4, 1.5e4, 3.2e4) instead of rising. In f_meas the cluster own cells near the fit end are near-zero navy while grey charge from two other tracks crosses the region in U and V, so the end sits in a coverage hole and rule 3 fails its no-hole clause. The chain offers S311019 as the Michel: 2 points over 0.4 cm at 1.3e4 e/cm, 10.0 cm out at cos_fwd -0.15, which shows in all three stop azimuths as a bare vertex marker with no cloud at all, so it is not topology either. With no readable profile in the last 15 cm, no arm and no exit, I cannot tell whether this muon stopped here, and I will not manufacture a verdict from an artifact wave.
notes: NO_MEASUREMENT: the last ~15 cm carries no measured charge and the whole panel is a smooth periodic wave with recurring zeros, so neither a rise nor a flat profile can be read. Rule 3 is unavailable because a coverage hole swallows the end. Competing readings I weighed: an OVERSHOOT (peak at s=17 then collapse) and a rule-3 FLAT_STOP; both are refused because the zero recurs at s=33-36 as well, which no single physical collapse does.

Past the stop the substantial object is 469046, a 23-point 13.2 cm track at 30433 e/cm, about half the muon plateau, whose near end is 15.6 cm out and which the three azimuths show clearly detached from the star by a charge-free gap and running at a large angle to the muon, with 469047 (2.3 cm, 66419) carrying it on to 28.5 cm. C474, 14 points 53 cm out, is 42.7 cm BACK along the muon and 33.8 cm off its body line by my own projection, i.e. on the wrong side of the stop and in an unrelated direction, so delta / other, as are the four pdg 11 shower pieces 136032-136041 which sit 513-534 cm away at the far anode end. evidence: 466 cm chain entering through the top at (120,587,271), 18.5 cm below y = 606, and ending at (83.6,190.0,97.6): d_face 97.4 cm to the z = 0.2 wall, 83.4 cm from the cathode, 268.5 cm from the anode, 133 cm from the z = 231 seam, in APA1 (x>0, z<231), so no exit route and no charge-deficit alibi. dy = -398 cm on a 435 cm chord, the fit end is the lower end. The profile climbs off its own 5.5e4 plateau to 7-8.5e4 over s = 10-30 cm, following the solid muon curve, dips to 1.3-5e4 for three or four points at s = 2-5, and then spikes to 1.0e5, 1.38e5 and 1.57e5 on the last three points, about 2.5 times plateau and sitting on the reference curve; the 3-D clouds show the same thing as a green-to-orange colour change over the last 15 cm. Ragged, but a rise, and the terminal spike is where a Bragg peak belongs. The track is shallow in drift - 37 cm of x over 466 cm of track, about 4.5 deg to the wire plane overall and about 6 deg locally at the stop - which is one reason the last few points scatter as they do, but it still spans some hundred time slices in f_meas rather than a few, so it is not the near-isochronous case the rubric excepts. Nothing attached at the stop leaves it: the three pieces past the end are all small and detached. S231016 is 2 points over 0.9 cm, 9.8 cm essentially straight out to the side of the stop (cos_fwd 0.06), carrying about 1.1e5 e/cm, i.e. roughly 3 MeV of charge. S229014 is 4 points over 1.7 cm, 7.6 cm forward and 9.7 cm to the other side, at 8.9e3 e/cm, under 1 MeV. S230015 is 3 points over 1.2 cm, 27 cm ahead and 12 cm off-axis, at 2.7e4 e/cm. All three are well clear of the body line, all are detached across a visible gap in the three stop azimuths, all are beyond the 5 cm within which a compact piece stays part of the Michel, and their combined charge is a few MeV, far short of a 35 MeV Michel and exactly what an isotropic capture cascade looks like, so all three are gamma and the item stays STM_ONLY. S86009, the chain delta, is 12 points over 6.4 cm attached at the S86007/S86010 vertex 5.3 cm before the stop and running back along the body at cos_fwd -0.99, with its centroid offset from the stop lying within a degree of the body direction: it hugs the body and does not start at the stop vertex, so delta / other. In f_meas the coloured cells end together in U, V and W; the grey bands in all three planes have slopes different from the track own and none picks up its line at the end.
notes: Medium, not high, because the verdict turns on STM_ONLY versus STM_MICHEL rather than on whether it stopped: the rise is unambiguous, but two of the three specks past the end are typed michel by the chain. I refused that reading because none of them attaches to the stop, each is only 1-2 cm long, and their combined charge is a few MeV against the ~35 MeV a Michel carries, which is the isotropic capture-gamma picture the rubric assigns to an STM_ONLY. The shallow drift angle (37 cm of x over 466 cm) is noted in the evidence but does not meet the rubric few-time-slices bar, so I did not stamp ISOCHRONOUS.

evidence: 150 cm near-vertical track in APA1 (x>0, z<231) lying at essentially constant z, 222.8 to 228.2. Two more independent reasons point the same way: face.x = 0.2 cm and seams_at_stop.anode_face = 0.2 cm put the end right on the x = +352.1 anode wire plane, and seam_z = 2.8 cm puts it within three centimetres of the z = 231 APA seam, either of which is an exit under rule 5 and the seam rule. The profile gives rule 7 nothing to overturn it: the plateau runs 5.0-6.0e4 over the whole 45 cm shown with the usual point-to-point scatter down to 4.2e4, and there is no climb at all towards s = 0, only one isolated 8.8e4 point at the very end which is the separate two-point piece 120016 (98486 e/cm, cos_fwd 1.0, 0.6 cm, chain-typed pdg 2212). One point at 1.6x plateau is not a clear rise, and a 0.6 cm stub running dead straight ahead is exactly the collinear stub that v2 says is not topology, so neither branch of rule 7 second bullet fires. THRU, and with three independent grounds it is high.
notes: DIRECTION: fit end is the upper end, dy = +141.7 cm over a 145.4 cm chord (0.97); ANODE: face.x = 0.2 cm; SEAM: 2.8 cm from the z = 231 APA seam

evidence: A short object: only 43.6 cm of chain in 71 points. The chain entry is at (-0.2,415.6,322.3), i.e. x = -0.2 against a cathode face at |x| = 0.16, so the upper end sits dead on the cathode and the rest of this muon is in the x>0 drift volume and in another cluster; that is why I call it a fragment. The fit end is at (-13.4,383.5,341.5), 13.2 cm from the cathode, 120.8 cm from the nearest wall, 338.7 cm from the anode and 110 cm from the z = 231 seam, in APA2 (x<0, z>232) but at y = 383, not the bad far-z bottom corner. dy = -32 cm on a 40 cm chord, so the fit end is the lower end and rule 7 does not bite. The profile cannot be read: every point lies on a smooth arc, rising from 0 at s = -4 to 5.2e4 at s = 0, peaking at 6.8e4 at s = 5, collapsing to 1.4e4 by s = 15, back up to 4e4 at s = 26, down to 1.8e4 at s = 33, up to 3.4e4 at s = 37 and to zero at s = 39. A physical dQ/dx does not oscillate with an 11 cm period and no scatter; this is the patchy-charge wave, and the whole object reads at half a normal plateau (segment means 2.3e4-3.0e4, and the chain own range-vs-dQ/dx energies disagree by a factor two, 130 vs 63 MeV), so neither a rise nor a flat reading is available. What decides it is topology: S68001 is a separate 15-point object attached at the stop vertex (d_min 0.0, d_max 4.44 cm) leaving at cos_fwd 0.27, i.e. about 72 deg off the muon local direction, and the kink is visible as a direction change in all three stop azimuths, with the piece running mostly in +z while the muon arrives going down in y. That is not the weak straight-on stub the rubric excludes, and its charge falls from 5.2e4 at the vertex to zero 4 cm out, which is what an electron does and not what a muon continuing does. So rule 1 fires: the muon stopped and S68001 is the Michel, about 4 cm of range, a ~10 MeV electron. The three pdg-11 shower pieces S68004, S68006 and S68008 are all 24-42 cm back at cos_fwd -0.95 or below, bunched at the cathode entry rather than at the stop, so they are delta / other; they are not a busy stop and rule 6 does not apply, since the last 20 cm before the fit end is clean.
notes: NO_MEASUREMENT: the dQ/dx panel is a smooth 11 cm-period wave with zero nodes, so the Bragg test is unavailable and the verdict rests entirely on the 4.4 cm kinked arm at the stop vertex. CATHODE: the chain entry is 0.0 cm from the cathode face, which is why the verdict carries FRAG. The competing reading is UNCLEAR, and in the U panel of f_meas a grey diagonal passes close to the fit end, but it does not pick up the track line at matching slices in V and W, so I did not call CONTINUES.

evidence: 415 cm chain in four segments. The chain entry is at (69,12,41), only 4.4 cm above the y=7.6 floor, and the fit end is at (352.0,284.3,122.9) with face.x = 0.1 cm and seams_at_stop.anode_face = 0.1 cm, i.e. sitting exactly on the anode wire plane at |x| = 352.1; d_face is 0.1 cm, and the end view of a_proj_full shows the track running straight into the red x boundary. dy = +272 cm on a 401 cm chord (0.68), so this is also the track upper end and rule 7 applies; the other end is on the floor, so neither end is a candidate stop. The dQ/dx profile over the last 45 cm is flat and scattered between 3.5e4 and 5.5e4 about a plateau near 5e4, with no climb at all towards s=0; if anything the last three points are slightly low, and the two hot red points at s=30-32 (1.35e5) are a delta 30 cm back, nowhere near the end. The only thing near the end is S315016, 2 points over 0.8 cm at 1.8e4 e/cm, about a third of plateau, 7.8 cm out at cos_fwd 0.31: it shows as a bare vertex marker with essentially no cloud in all three stop azimuths, which is a faint speck and not a clear electron arm, so rule 7 second bullet is not satisfied. In f_meas the coloured cells stop cleanly at slice ~170 in U, V and W with no grey picking up the line below it; the grey diagonals crossing the U and W panels run the other way and are other tracks, and the V dead band at channel ~4510 is 110 channels clear of the track. Stop is in the x>0, z<231 quadrant (APA1), so neither the APA0 nor the APA2 deficit applies. THRU: an anode exit at the upper end.
notes: ANODE: face.x = 0.1 cm, the end is on the wire plane. DIRECTION: dy = +272 on a 401 cm chord, the fit end is the upper end and the chain entry is 4.4 cm off the floor. The chain offers S315016 as the Michel; at 2 points, 0.8 cm and a third of plateau charge it is a speck, not topology.

evidence: A 12.2 cm, 22-point stub, the whole drawn cluster, sitting against the x = -352.1 anode in APA0 (x<0, z = 26.8). The chain entry is at (-351.4, 389.9, 23.8) with face.x = 0.7 cm, i.e. ON the anode wire plane, and the fit end at (-342.6, 383.2, 26.8) is 9.5 cm in from it; 222.8 cm from the top, 26.6 cm from the z front face, 204 cm from the seam and 342 cm from the cathode. dy = -6.7 over an 11.5 cm chord (0.58) so the fit end is nominally the lower end and rule 7 does not bite, but the direction test is nearly meaningless on a 12 cm object. The profile is unreadable: 22 points scattered between 0.9e4 and 6.9e4 over the whole 12 cm with no plateau and no trend, the last points at s = 0-1 sitting at 1.3-2.9e4, among the lowest in the set, and the two chain segments carry 48033 (3.4-10.8 cm out) then 31772 (0-3.4 cm), i.e. the charge falls towards the fit end rather than rising. That is rule 4 territory, not a flat profile. What decides the item is f_meas. In all three planes this object own coloured cells sit embedded in a much longer grey track that runs straight through them and carries on past the fit end at matching time slices: in W a long grey diagonal from about (6870, 730) to (7070, 550) with the own cells at (6925-6945, 665-705) lying exactly on it; in U a grey diagonal from about (705, 655) to (815, 850) with the own cells at (710-730, 665-705) on its lower end; in V a near-vertical grey line at V 3420-3445 spanning slices 550-850 with the own cells occupying only slices 670-705 of it. Same line, same direction, three planes, matching slices - that is the v4 definition of a continuation, not grey merely crossing the region. So the drawn cluster is one 12 cm piece of a long track the clustering broke up, the verdict describes the full object, and it is FRAG_THRU. The three 3-D azimuths show nothing else at all in the 45 cm ball (the rest of the object is in another cluster and therefore hidden), and the object table has only the two fitted muon rows, so there is no topology to weigh. Both rows tagged muon, kind none.
notes: CONTINUES: the fit end line is picked up by grey charge in all three planes at matching slices and runs on for 100-200 channels; NO_MEASUREMENT: 22 points over 12.2 cm, nothing readable

evidence: 134 cm curving chain entering through the top at (-240,604,347), 1.9 cm below y = 606, and ending at (-311.4,531.7,271.0): nearest face is the anode at 40.7 cm, 74.3 cm from the y wall, 191 cm from the z wall, 40.0 cm from the z = 231 seam and 311 cm from the cathode, in APA2 (x<0, z>232) but at y = 532, not the bad bottom corner. dy = -72 cm on a 127 cm chord, so the fit end is the lower end and rule 7 does not bite; the end is deep enough that no face, seam or cathode is a possible exit. The profile is the awkward part. It sits on a 6-7e4 plateau out at s = 32-45, swells into a broad bump that peaks at 1.5-1.65e5 (about 2.5 times plateau) at s = 20-22, and then falls back through 1.15e5 at s = 15 to 7e4 by s = 12, staying at 6-7.5e4 flat over the last 13 cm; the hot stretch shows in the 3-D frames as a dark-red section of the arc with green plateau on both sides of it. A Bragg peak does not come back down, so I read the bump as a local enhancement (an overlapping object or a hard delta), not a terminal peak, and I did not move the pin: the rubric overshoot signature needs the post-peak segment to collapse well below plateau, and this one sits exactly on plateau. So the profile at the fit end is flat, and since all of rule 3 conditions hold - the charge ends in all three planes of f_meas, no dead band or hole swallows it, the end is 40.7 cm from the anode, 40.0 from the seam and 311 from the cathode, nothing continues past it, and it is the lower end - a flat profile here is a measurement failure and not a through-goer. Rule 1 then decides what kind of stop. S42002 is attached at the stop vertex (d_min 0.0, d_max 3.0 cm), 7 points over 3.5 cm leaving at cos_fwd 0.03, i.e. about 88 deg to the muon, and its own points fall from 4.7e4 at the vertex to 0.2e4 three cm out - charge below plateau and falling outwards, which is a Michel and not a muon last centimetres. It is not the weak straight-on stub the rubric excludes. Past it, S174008 is a 2-point 0.2 cm blob 9.4 cm out (8.3 cm of that transverse), S173007 a 3-point 1.0 cm blob 13.4 cm out and 12.3 cm forward, and S172006 a 2-point speck 29.8 cm out at cos_fwd 0.92: all compact, all detached across a clear gap, all clear of the body line and all inside the 60 cm gamma radius on the Michel side, so gamma. I checked the undershoot case and rejected it: the two hot blobs carry 1.6 and 2.0 times plateau rather than several times, they sit 9 and 13 cm out rather than 1-3 cm, and there is no muon charge at all bridging the gap to them. S42005 is the chain delta 101-103 cm back along the body at cos_fwd -0.97: delta / other. In f_meas the coloured cells terminate in U, V and W, with the charge of these four objects showing as grey just beyond the end; the nearest U dead bands are 75+ channels away, though a thin dead W channel sits about 10 channels past the end.
notes: FLAT_STOP: the last 13 cm sits flat on plateau with no rise, but the end is 40.7 cm from the anode, 40.0 cm from the seam, 311 cm from the cathode, its charge ends in all three planes, nothing continues past it and it is the lower end, so rule 3 makes the missing rise a measurement failure rather than a through-goer. This is what caps the call at medium: the verdict rests on rule 1, an attached 3 cm perpendicular arm whose charge falls outwards, with no Bragg rise to corroborate. Competing reading is THRU, refused for the reasons above, and OVERSHOOT with the pin near s = 16, refused because the post-bump charge sits on plateau instead of collapsing below it. Tag doubt: S174008 at 9.4 cm lies roughly along S42002 direction and could be michel rather than gamma; the kind stays both either way because of S173007 and S172006.

evidence: This is not one track. The object table alone has 49 rows in 4 groups - 15 muon segments, 2 michel, 4 delta, 28 unassigned pdg 11 shower pieces - plus 5 more blobs from another flash, and b_3d_wide shows exactly that: a bush of a dozen differently-coloured PR segments leaving in all directions (pink, brown, orange, purple, yellow, green), some forty opaque vertex squares, and a diffuse point cloud that fills the whole 45 cm ball, not a spine. The chain runs 166 cm of fit over a 94 cm entry-to-stop chord, i.e. it wanders badly, and its own segments carry dqdx from 5744 to 77136 e/cm, a factor of thirteen along what is supposed to be one minimum-ionising muon. Geometry: chain entry at (-51.9, 405.4, 7.9), 7.6 cm from the z = 0.2 front face, fit end at (-69.7, 376.4, 95.4) in APA0 (x<0, z<231), 95.2 cm from the nearest face, 69.5 cm from the cathode, 135.6 cm from the seam, so containment is fine and no face, cathode or seam explains anything. dy = -29.0 over a 93.9 cm chord, a ratio of 0.31 downward, so it is nominally the lower end and rule 7 does not bite, but the track is close to flat and close to isochronous (x moves only 17.8 cm), which the rubric flags as making ends unreliable. The profile cannot be read: it is the APA0 weak-collection wave the v3 note names, a smooth sawtooth with a ~10 cm period that repeatedly touches zero and peaks at only 4e4, well under the reference curve everywhere, so there is no plateau to measure a rise against and rule 2 has nothing to say. At the stop itself I cannot isolate anything: 26049, a 21-point 12.3 cm pdg 11 shower piece, starts at d_min 0.0 on the stop vertex, 26043 is a 69-point 41 cm shower piece 20-34 cm out, and six vertex squares sit within a few centimetres of the star in the c and d azimuths. That is rule 6 word for word - a large object running along and across the track near its end so that I cannot tell where this track ends or what leaves it. f_meas is the same picture: the own cells form a broad band in W rather than a line, brown vertex markers are scattered right across the frame, and two large grey V-shaped tracks cross the region. Every row is tagged delta / other and the kind is none, as the rubric requires for MESSY.
notes: NO_MEASUREMENT: the dQ/dx is the APA0 patchy-collection wave, a 10 cm sawtooth between ~0 and 4e4 with nothing readable; ISOCHRONOUS: x moves only 17.8 cm over a 94 cm chord and the W cells sit in a 70-slice band

evidence: A short, isolated, slightly hooked 12.8 cm track of 22 points in APA2 (x<0, z = 440.6) at y = 311-316, well away from the APA2 bottom-corner hole. Entry (-213.0, 311.1, 443.2), 18.8 cm inside the z = 462 back face; fit end (-222.1, 316.0, 440.6), 21.7 cm from that face, 290 cm from the top and bottom, 130.0 cm from the anode and 221.9 cm from the cathode, and 209.6 cm from the seam - so no face, anode, cathode or seam is anywhere near either end. The profile is the cleanest Bragg curve in my set: 22 points climbing smoothly and monotonically from 4.0e4 at s = 13 through 5.5e4 at s = 9, 7.0e4 at s = 5, 9.0e4 at s = 2 to 1.05e5 at the fit last point, tracking the muon reference curve almost point for point, and the 3-D colouring shows the same (blue at the far end, green-yellow into the star). The track also bends over its last few centimetres in the d azimuth, which is what a muon scattering at the end of its range does. Nothing whatever sits past the star in any of the three azimuths and the object table has only the two fitted muon rows, 28002 the chain and 28001 at 8.7-10.3 cm out at the FAR end, so there is no decay activity and the verdict is STM_ONLY, not STM_MICHEL. Two things hold the confidence to medium. First, rule 7: dy = +4.9 over a 10.66 cm chord is 0.46, so this is the track UPPER end and a stop here needs an upward-going particle; the v5 second bullet says a clear rise still makes it a stop but caps confidence, and I cannot say where the muon came from since no lower continuation is drawn. Second, f_meas is not clean: in W the own cells at channels 9230-9240, slices 928-958 sit on a long steep grey line that runs from about (9205, 780) to (9260, 1060), which taken alone would read as a continuation. I did not call CONTINUES because the rubric requires the line to be carried in all three planes at matching slices and it is not: in U the own cells run at about one slice per channel while the two grey tracks crossing there run at +2.2 and -0.6, and in V the own cells sit against a dead-channel band so that plane can say nothing. A through-goer also cannot produce a monotonic climb to twice plateau at the exact point its fit stops, so I let rule 2 decide.
notes: DIRECTION: the fit end is the upper end, dy = +4.9 cm over a 10.66 cm chord (0.46), so rule 7 caps this at medium; kept a stop under the v5 second bullet because the Bragg rise is textbook

evidence: 235 cm chain in four segments. The stop is in APA2 (x<0, z>232) but at y = 115 rather than the bad far-z bottom corner, and f_meas shows the predicted band covered by measured charge all the way down, so this is not a coverage hole. The dQ/dx profile is flat over the last 45 cm, scattering 3.5e4 to 6.5e4 about a plateau near 5.5e4 with no climb towards s=0; the last four points are if anything 20 percent below plateau. All the structure is 36-52 cm back up the track: S52007 (10.1 cm at 9.6e4), the delta S52009 and the 9.9 cm shower piece S52003, which show as the hot 8e4-1.1e5 points at s = 27-45 and as the orange markers at s = -37 to -40; that is a hard delta/shower 40 cm back, not an end. Nothing at all sits within 36 cm of the fit end: the three stop azimuths show the cloud terminating abruptly at the pin with no arm and no separate piece, and in f_meas the coloured cells end together at slice ~390 in U, V and W with no grey carrying the line on. C227 is 54 cm out at cos_fwd -0.35 with no dqdx value, a degenerate row. THRU: an anode exit at the upper end.
notes: ANODE: face.x = 0.2 cm, the end is on the wire plane. DIRECTION: dy = +101 on a 224 cm chord, the fit end is the upper end and the chain entry is 7.0 cm off the floor. The U panel dead band at channel ~1858 sits right beside the last U cells, but the V and W ends are clean and the anode geometry settles it.
